rows.practice_entry: 22. A kill that attributes to nothing is a pass — the same output, two diseases, on the other side
rows.notes: This IS the mutation engine (8,690 lines): manifest-driven mutations, kill attribution by parsing each guard's --self-test output, the cost-balanced shard partition (sweep_shard / sweep_partition) and the import-closure selection (select_manifests). Spec 2c reads C3 against GitHub Actions plus an ARBITRARY mutation engine, so shipping this engine as the CI layer's dependency is the C3 failure the spec names; the plan expects DON'T-SHIP with a practice harvest. C3 fail, argued from spec 2c (line 152: depending on our engine is a C3 failure, and this component IS the engine) and from HARNESS_TREE (line 471), the allow-list of this repo's directories every mutation run stages (scripts, supabase, docs, node_modules/typescript); the scan emitted NO finding for HARNESS_TREE (a scan bound). Ground (spec 5 rule 1, amended 2026-11-22 by the owner, option A): the scope decision of spec 3 Effort (2) (line 363: the mutation engine itself, check-plan-code.py --mutate and scripts/mutations/, is the expected DON'T-SHIP) and spec 2c's reading of C3 for a CI piece (line 152). No scan finding is named as a ground, because none bears on this verdict: check-plan-code:2:1 (line 2494) is detector 2's `unread` kind, one of ten loads the reader could not resolve, which check-publishability.py calls an unjudged coupling, shown and never counted as none; it is not evidence of a repo path; :6:3 bears on the C2 PASS below; and these are self-test internals that do not bear on a stranger's run: :4:1 and :4:2 (lines 8162, 8165, the self-test's _copy_run writing and running a copy of this file) and :6:1 (line 3995, the self-test saving and restoring PC495_STATE, a variable that same test sets for its fake suite). C2 pass, argued: :6:3 reads GITHUB_ACTIONS, which GitHub Actions provides, and no Supabase/Gemini/Fly edge was emitted. C4 fail, argued: every mutation is a hand-written manifest anchored to one of THIS repo's guards, so a stranger's repository has nothing for it to mutate. Practice harvest: section 22 (kill attribution through parsed output) exists; section 10 (a surviving mutation first asks whether the guard can fire) is a second candidate. Practices with NO heading yet (left for Task 20, not claimed here): cost-balanced sharding with a loud round-robin fallback; selecting suites by import closure. Costs: public bar = make it engine-agnostic (a manifest format any repo can author, no repo-path constants, a documented record schema); next project = copy it and re-anchor manifests to that project's guards.

Pieces (a) matrix sharding and (c) the scheduled full sweep live here: the mutation-sweep job (.github/workflows/ci.yml line 1117) is a 38-shard matrix (max-parallel 12 on the schedule), the nightly cron is '30 8 * * *', and the mutation-sweep-complete step runs scripts/sweep-red-alert.py. C3 fail, argued from the three scan findings inside the sweep's jobs (mutation-sweep runs from ci.yml line 1117 to 1532, mutation-sweep-complete from line 1533): :2:106 (line 1432, outside-set scripts/check-python-pin.py), :2:107 (line 1515, cwd-relative check-plan-code --mutate) and :2:108 (line 1628, cwd-relative sweep-red-alert.py) call this repo's scripts by repo-relative path; a `uses:` caller's checkout has none of them. C2 pass, argued: the sweep steps need only GitHub Actions, Python and git. C4 fail, argued (spec 2c: C4 stays argued, no experiment): there is no reusable-workflow file to put on a `uses:` line yet. Bound: this component is the WHOLE ci.yml, so 105 of its 108 scan findings (every one before line 1117) are steps of the verify job and do not bear on the sweep; only 3 of 108 are at line 1117 or later. Route: extract the job into a reusable workflow with `on: workflow_call` whose inputs name the caller's mutation command, shard count and schedule-driven budget; the engine becomes an input, which is what spec 2c's C3 asks. harvest none: no portable-practices heading covers sharding or the scheduled sweep (a candidate for Task 20). Engine comparison for pieces (a) and (c): the top-level engine_comparison list.

Piece (c)'s alert: reads every shard's record and opens or comments on a `sweep-red` (and `sweep-flaky`) issue, never closing one. At runtime (main, line 197, and its helpers) it needs only the standard library and `gh` through subprocess (line 189); it loads neither the engine nor coverage_verdict. C3 fail, argued from the record contract: RECORD_SCHEMA = 1 (line 58) is the schema check-plan-code.shard_record writes (check-plan-code.py line 2988), and record_problem (line 88) accepts exactly the five keys of RECORD_KEYS, so the runtime reader is bound to our engine's record format; and the shipped file's --self-test cannot run without the engine. Ground (spec 5 rule 1): sweep-red-alert:4:1 (line 332), _writer(), the self-test's importlib load of check-plan-code.py (called at line 441), which is the self-test's dependency on the engine and so grounds the second reason; the record-contract reason is argued from the lines above, on which the scan emitted no finding (the scan emitted none on the runtime path). Two other findings are inside _self_test_body (lines 339 to 592) and are NOT grounds, because resolving either would change neither reason: :2:1 (line 496) runs the alert step's run block, read from this repo's ci.yml, against a fake gh, and :6:1 (line 471) is the self-test's git, building a throwaway repository. C2 pass, argued: at runtime the only external program is `gh`, authenticated by the Actions token, which a GitHub runner has; git (:6:1) is used only by the self-test. Route, re-priced because no engine load happens at runtime: ship inside the same reusable workflow, publish RECORD_SCHEMA and the five keys as the documented record contract that any engine's wrapper writes, and replace the self-test's engine-written records (_writer) with literal fixture records. harvest none: no heading for the scheduled-sweep alert pattern exists.

engine_comparison.scope: plan Task 17: pieces (a) matrix sharding, (b) selection by closure / observed reach, (c) scheduled full sweep with a sweep-red issue, against the incremental and shard modes of Stryker, mutmut, PIT and cargo-mutants, from each project's own documentation fetched 2026-11-22 (the pages cited in sentences changed by review round 1 were re-fetched the same day). 'Not documented' means not found IN THE PAGES LISTED, not that the engine lacks it.

ours.a: check-plan-code.py sweep_shard / sweep_partition: N shards of equal ESTIMATED cost from scripts/sweep-costs.json, round-robin when no costs table; ci.yml mutation-sweep matrix of 38 shards.
ours.b: check-plan-code.py select_manifests: on a PR, selects the guard SUITES (manifests) whose import closure the diff reaches; observed-reach selection (backlog #586, strace) is in progress and not in the components map.
ours.c: ci.yml cron '30 8 * * *' runs the full sweep; sweep-red-alert.py opens or comments on a sweep-red issue.

rows.capability: Parallelism is a `concurrency` count of worker processes on one machine; sharding one run across CI jobs is not documented in the fetched pages.
Runs mutants in parallel worker processes on one machine; sharding across jobs is not documented in the fetched pages.
A `threads` option on one machine; sharding across jobs is not documented in the fetched pages.

`--shard k/n` splits mutants across independent jobs, assigned by contiguous slice (the default) or round-robin with `--sharding`, with no coordination between shards; the page gives a GitHub Actions matrix example and says the CI system launches the shards and collects their results. Ours differs in partitioning by estimated cost rather than by count.

StrykerJS `--incremental` reuses results from reports/stryker-incremental.json and re-tests mutants in changed mutated or test files, using a git-like diff and the mutation coverage per test its dry run records; the page says it will not detect changes in files other than mutated files and test files. Selection is of MUTANTS by file diff, with tests chosen per mutant by observed coverage, not of suites by import closure.

Stryker.NET `since` uses git information to test only code changes since the given target and reports only on mutants within the changed code; for a changed test file, all mutants covered by tests in that file are seen as changed. `with-baseline` saves the report so a partial run still yields a full report.

Between runs it re-tests only mutants in functions whose source changed, and can be limited by name globs or `only_mutate`; it 'knows which tests to execute' from a stats run of the suite, counting a test as relevant for a function only if the stack depth is below a limit (`max_stack_depth`), which is test selection by runtime-observed reach per function; a git-diff or import-closure selection is not documented in the fetched pages.

Experimental incremental analysis via history files reuses a result when the class under test and the killing test are unchanged, tracking only its strongest dependencies (superclasses, outer classes); import-closure selection of suites is not documented in the fetched pages.

Under 'Integrating pitest into pull requests', the example `-DextraFeatures="+GIT(from[HEAD~1]), +arcmutate_history(...)"` is said to 'activate arcmutate's git integration and history implementations', and Arcmutate 'provides pull request integration and other advanced features'; the page does not explain what +GIT selects, and does not say the feature moved from PIT.
`--in-diff` tests only mutants overlapping changed regions of a diff and ignores test-code changes; the page says it is not a substitute for a full test run.
`--iterate` skips mutants caught in a previous run, described as a heuristic.

Pipeline use is a break threshold (`--break-at`) that fails the pipeline below a mutation score, and a dashboard baseline for pull requests (`--with-baseline`, `--dashboard-api-key`, `"provider": "Dashboard"`) that tests only mutations changed against a target such as master; sending a report to the dashboard is documented on https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/General/dashboard/ ('Send your first report directly from Stryker'); a scheduled sweep or filing an issue is not documented in the fetched pages.
Offers `export-cicd-stats` and a badge; a scheduled sweep or filing an issue is not documented in the fetched pages.
A `mutationThreshold` fails the build; a scheduled sweep or filing an issue is not documented in the fetched pages.

Shows one workflow, on pushes to main and on path-filtered pull requests, whose single job runs a full `cargo mutants -vV --in-place` and emits GitHub annotations; a diff-focused PR check is only linked (pr-diff.html, not fetched, so no claim rests on it); a cron schedule or filing an issue is not documented in the fetched pages.

conclusions: a: in the fetched pages, only cargo-mutants documents sharding one run across CI jobs (https://mutants.rs/shards.html); its assignment is by count (slice or round-robin, each shard the same number of mutants +/-1), ours by estimated cost. This is an absence in the pages listed, not across each engine's whole documentation.

b: in the fetched pages, all four document selecting MUTANTS by what changed (file, function, class or diff region), and mutmut (stack-depth-bounded test relevance per function, https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) and Stryker (mutation coverage per test, https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/incremental/) choose the tests run per mutant by runtime-observed coverage, the nearest equivalent to our observed-reach piece, which is not in the components map; none of the fetched pages documents selecting test SUITES by the import closure of a change.

c: none of the fetched pages documents a scheduled full sweep that files an issue; cargo-mutants' full run on push to main (https://mutants.rs/ci.html) is the nearest. This is an absence in the pages listed, not across each engine's whole documentation.
